races.name: JenningsBet In Bexhill On Sea Apprentice Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: Boyle-trained 4yo who has been running consistently over 6f on good ground but is now stepped to 7f; her natural hold-up style is compromised in this field of similarly-minded closers, and Owen Lewis takes a 5lb claim — sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 comparable runs is uninspiring.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, Apple's Angel at least has experience over today's trip and going, and 30 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; however, 135 lb from stall one is a notable ask for a filly rated just 45.

runners_data.name: Barnsnape Boy
runners_data.note: Boyle's second string here, but the stronger case on paper — three wins from 13 runs on good going at 7f tells a clear story, and Donagh Murphy's 5lb claim preserves a competitive weight; a natural closer by trade, he is one of the more adaptable hold-up horses in the field and can travel prominently when needed.|
runners_data.comment: Barnsnape Boy has managed just one win in his last six starts, finishing eighth last time out, and our rating ranks him last of the eight runners here. He has run over today's trip and going before, and 15 days since his last outing suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Carroll-trained 5yo who operates over 5-6f typically, now up to 7f; the redistribution to the lead reflects his status as the only plausible pace-setter, but this trip is a query and Matthew Lloyd Slater's 5lb claim does not compensate for a horse racing beyond his likely comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: Port Hedland won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine contender from stall 3 at 135 lb — though his two subsequent runs since that victory, including a fifth last time, suggest he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (LR:1d) which is a significant freshness concern and demands scrutiny; the 8yo has a win at 8f on good ground in his history and is equipped with headgear, but form figures of 606851 across 7-8f on varying ground make him an erratic proposition — Molly Gunn's 5lb claim is the headline angle.|
runners_data.comment: River Wharfe arrives here on the back of a win last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, making him a live threat from stall two; the obvious query is whether he can back it up having run just yesterday.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Carroll's third runner in the race, a 4yo whose recent form string of 988066 speaks for itself; the headgear flag is noted and Myla Coppins claims 5lbs, but the sim-going record (0 wins, 3 places) and string of poor runs at 7-8f on good ground make it hard to construct a confident case.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and running again just a day after his most recent sixth, Rock Master faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a draw of five is his most neutral angle.

runners_data.name: Spirited Dancer
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts from his last three runs, including a 2nd at 7f on good, mark him out as a horse in competitive form; held up by nature but mapped to midfield given the volume of closers here — his Kubler trainer yard is 4 from 11 over 14 days, and Warren Fentiman rides without a claim but adds experience.|
runners_data.comment: Spirited Dancer has placed twice in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating has her narrowly on top — the main concern is that she's been out of the frame in her last two outings and remains winless in recent form.

runners_data.name: Valadero
runners_data.note: Toomey-trained 5yo who placed at 6f on good most recently; a 41-day absence is a mild query, and his sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 runs on comparable ground is a deterrent — Liam Wright rides without a claim and this horse's best effort came over 6f, making the 7f test another reservation.|
runners_data.comment: Valadero showed a return to form when third last time out after a run of disappointing efforts, and he has experience of today's distance and going. Winless in his last five starts, but carrying 135 lb from stall six, the 41-day break looks a positive.

runners_data.name: Voodoo Ray
runners_data.note: A 7yo lightly raced in recent months (49 days off) with no wins or places on similar going across five comparable runs; Jude Fernandes' 7lb claim is notable but the form figures of 49-704 on his recent starts, combined with a natural deep-closing style that is undermined by this race shape, make him difficult to support.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 49 days, Voodoo Ray does at least bring distance and going experience to the table; carrying 135 lb from stall four, his fourth last time out hints at some residual form, though he remains hard to trust at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Port Hedland is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 7f Brighton contest, redistributed to the lead from a prominent profile, and with no genuine front-runner to push against, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on good-to-firm ground. The absence of any natural front-runner means the tempo is unlikely to be fierce, which typically compresses the field and makes it harder for true hold-up horses to produce a telling late burst. Every other runner in this field — Valadero, Spirited Dancer, Barnsnape Boy, Apple's Angel, Rock Master and Voodoo Ray — has been redistributed from hold-up positions into midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for the race shape to accommodate them all at the rear; those most capable of adapting, such as Barnsnape Boy (3 wins on similar going at 7f) and Spirited Dancer (two recent placed efforts), are the likeliest to push into a competitive midfield berth. The race shape therefore favours horses who can sit just off the pace in the first half of the field and pick off a lone, unextended leader, with genuine deep closers at a significant disadvantage given the soft gallop and the bunching that follows.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Track Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Port Hedland dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the midfield clusters together without disruption.
scenarios.body: Port Hedland's lone lead at a comfortable tempo means stamina is preserved rather than tested, and the race becomes a sprint from 2f out, rewarding horses who track just off the pace. Barnsnape Boy and Spirited Dancer, who have the form to race prominently when circumstances demand, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested early gallop is genuinely slow and creates a wall-to-wall finishing sprint off the home turn.
scenarios.body: A crawl early compresses the field entirely, turning the race into a dash over the final 2f where horses with a high top-speed rating and finishing kick outpoint the leader. Spirited Dancer's back-to-back placed efforts on similar ground and Valadero's course-relevant form at 6f on good give them the profile to thread through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Port Hedland settles into a measured rhythm that suits his stamina and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Port Hedland's front-running redistribution only works if no horse tracks him closely enough to apply pressure at the 2f pole, allowing him to simply outstay a scrambling, disorganised finish. River Wharfe's wider experience over 7-8f and her headgear flag suggest she could be the one shape capable of going with him to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly brisk early pace develops and hold-up horses — most of whom are redistributed — manage to find their natural position at the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario is significantly undermined by the fact that almost every hold-up type in the field has been pushed into midfield on the map, meaning few can realistically drop out and produce a clean run from off the pace. Apple's Angel and Voodoo Ray have the most natural late-running profiles but their recent form figures are poor and their style-fit scores reflect the compromise they face.

watchPoints.text: Barnsnape Boy's three wins on good going at 7f are the most directly relevant form credentials in this field — watch whether Murphy can slot him just off Port Hedland's back, as that is the position that turns his profile into a winning one.

River Wharfe ran just one day ago; monitor any market move as a positive drift would suggest connections themselves are cautious, and a horse returning this quickly on fast ground at Brighton deserves scrutiny in the parade ring.

Port Hedland is being asked to front-run over 7f having run his entire recent career at 5-6f — if he fails to stride on leaving the stalls, the entire race loses its confirmed pace source and the shape collapses into a bunched sprint with no clear tactical narrative.
Spirited Dancer's trainer Daniel & Claire Kubler yard is 4 from 11 in the past 14 days — a hot spell worth noting given his competitive recent placed form at this trip and going.

Three Tony Carroll runners (Port Hedland, River Wharfe, Rock Master) share the same yard; watch for any stable whisper indicating which is the intended runner, as yard form of 4 from 40 over 14 days is modest and tactical stable management may influence deployment.

races.name: JenningsBet Ladies Day Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
JenningsBet In Hastings Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dandy G Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who should slot in just behind the leader; Warren Greatrex's 14-day strike rate is modest at 1/11, and similar-going form reads 0 wins from 6 tries, but he placed second over this course-and-distance type profile and handles the conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Dandy G Boy shaped with promise when second three starts back and brings both distance and going experience to this assignment, making him a genuine threat off a weight of 135 lb — though consecutive sixth-place finishes last two outings are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Boubyan
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a solid record on Good ground at 8-10f, including a recent third over 8f and second over 8f on this going type; Michael Appleby's yard is 1/29 in the last fortnight, so confidence from the yard is limited, but the style suits a race where the pace collapses late — which is the least likely shape here.|
runners_data.comment: Boubyan has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out — with a second four starts back — shows he retains ability at this level despite being winless in recent starts; the main risk is a trainer in distinctly lean form at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: The most proven closer in the field with 1 win and 4 places from 7 similar-going runs, including a recent win over 10f Good and a second over 10f Good; Tom Queally will be forced to hold up and wait for a gap, but the uncontested pace from Danehill Star works against this runner's need for a strong early fractions.|
runners_data.comment: Gone Rogue won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a strong contender from stall 3 off 134 lb; the fourth last time out is the one minor concern, but his rating edge over his rivals marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who commands the race from flag to finish; Tony Carroll's yard is in good form at 4/40 over 14 days, William Carson partners him, and seven similar-going runs produce 0 wins but 6 places — a model of consistency at the front that suits today's solo-leader scenario perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Danehill Star has been competitive without winning in his last five starts, with one win in his last six, and our rating ranks him fifth of six here. Carrying 131 lb, he faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: Second Carroll runner in the race, suggesting the stable is double-handed and this nine-year-old is expected to track the lead; 0 wins but 1 place from 3 similar-going runs is modest, yet his pattern of prominent racing and recent placed efforts at 7-8f means he is stylistically well-suited to track Danehill Star throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kondratiev Wave faces a stiff ask here; he has experience over today's trip and going, returns fit on 17 days' rest, and a second last time out at least suggests he can get competitive.

runners_data.name: Winemaker
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has been busy (4/31 in 14 days) but this horse's natural running style is hold-up, and it arrives here genuinely displaced — it will be closer to the pace than ideal, with sprint-distance form on Tapeta and Standard making the Good to Firm mile over Brighton's hills a fitness and stamina question as much as a positional one.|
runners_data.comment: Winemaker showed he can compete at this level with a third two starts back, and has experience over today's trip and conditions from stall one carrying 125 lb; the concern is that seventh last time out suggests he needs to bounce back sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Danehill Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, William Carson can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating mile. Kondratiev Wave and Dandy G Boy will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a small but organised lead group rather than a contested, pressure-cooker pace. The hold-up horses — Boubyan, Gone Rogue, and Winemaker — will be stationed in the rear half, needing the pace to be either honest enough to string out the field or collapse late enough to produce a stamina test. Because Danehill Star faces no serious early pressure, this race is most likely to be run at a metronomic, front-runner-friendly tempo that rewards those able to travel close to the pace rather than those waiting off it; prominently placed runners who can pick up efficiently on Good to Firm ground hold the clearest positional advantage. The field does contain more hold-up types than the pace map can show at the rear — Winemaker is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map — meaning its natural closing position is unlikely to be available in a steadily-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danehill Star Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Danehill Star settles into a comfortable solo lead and Carson manages the tempo to suit, draining pace from the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Danehill Star dictates every yard, denying the closers a target to run at, and the Good to Firm surface rewards his clean stride pattern at this distance; the finish becomes a test of who has tracked closest to him throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy G Boy or Kondratiev Wave press Danehill Star hard enough through the final two furlongs to peg him back on the climb.
scenarios.body: The pace held by Danehill Star proves fractionally too slow to stop the prominent trackers finishing with more momentum, and one of them edges past near the line on the undulating Brighton finish; this requires the leader to have given just enough to the early pressure-free tempo that his reserves deplete late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Danehill Star sets a genuinely strong gallop that strings out the field and exposes the front-runners' stamina in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Gone Rogue and Boubyan, who both carry recent good-ground form at this sort of trip, are able to close strongly over the final two furlongs as the lead group falters; this scenario requires the pace to have been truly honest from the start, which is unlikely given the sole front-runner faces zero pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Winemaker Overcomes Position
scenarios.trigger: If Winemaker, racing out of its natural hold-up role in a compressed midfield, manages to find clear running and produce a sustained late effort.
scenarios.body: Its short-side sprint form on different tracks and surfaces makes it a doubtful stayer over this mile on Good to Firm turf, and being pushed out of its natural rearward position further reduces the probability of it finding the rhythm it needs; a big run is possible but the style-fit discount and unfamiliar trip combine to make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Danehill Star sets a falsely slow early gallop — if Carson finds no pressure and idles in front, the prominent trackers Kondratiev Wave and Dandy G Boy could be coasting well within themselves and overhaul him in the final furlong.

Winemaker's redistribution to midfield means it will not find the natural late run it relies on — watch whether Finley Marsh pushes forward early to compensate, which could disrupt the settled order behind Danehill Star.

Gone Rogue has the best similar-going profile in the field (1W4P from 7) but needs a stronger pace than Danehill Star is likely to set; if the gallop is flat, Tom Queally's challenge may arrive too late on the Brighton uphill finish.

Kondratiev Wave and Dandy G Boy are both Carroll and Greatrex prominent types — if they race each other for the secondary position they could burn more energy than ideal in a small field, marginally benefitting the front-runner and the closers alike.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race; all six runners are rated OK for going, but Boubyan's last five runs are exclusively on Good ground and Winemaker's history is predominantly on artificial surfaces — monitor market moves for clues on stable confidence.

races.name: JenningsBet In Basingstoke Brighton Challenge Cup Handicap Stakes (For The Brighton Challenge Cup) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Nibras Gold
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with a recent win and outstanding record on Good/Good-to-Firm ground (13/15); carries the toughperfect combination of experience at 8 and course fitness, but will face a direct early challenge from Tai Hang Pegasus for the lead.
runners_data.comment: Nibras Gold arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a second two starts back — a gelding in fine fettle who has experience of today's trip and conditions. Carrying 141 lb is the one test, but his recent form makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Maasai Mara
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needs things to go wrong for others to land a blow; 55 days off the track is a concern, and his similar-going record (7/15, 0 wins) does little to inspire confidence on this surface over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Maasai Mara shaped well for a second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 85 marking him out as the one to beat among these six — the risk is that he's winless in recent starts and a 55-day absence leaves fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: Exciting four-year-old in sharp form with three recent wins at 12f on Good ground; Finley Marsh's claim is relevant at the weights and Richard Hughes' string is in decent form (4/31 in 14 days), making this a compelling each-way profile sitting just off the likely pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Sarangpur carries 139 lb and faces a stiff task on these ratings, yet his recent form is genuinely solid — a winner last time out and a winner three starts back, with distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Top-rated in the field at OR=80 and a consistent placer, though still seeking a first win; races prominently and visors fitted could sharpen him up, but the yard is cold (0/7 in 14 days) and the step back up to 14f on a sharp track is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Brave Hunter shaped with promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating edging above his official mark suggesting he retains more ability than his recent efforts show — the main concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Breeze
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 10f on Good ground, but both came over a shorter trip than today's 14f; the hold-up style needs strong pace ahead and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps offset a low OR of 64, though stamina for this trip is genuinely unproven.
runners_data.comment: Bohemian Breeze arrives on the back of consecutive wins and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked bottom of this field on our figures with a speed rating of 60, he faces a stiff task off an official rating of 64.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Front-running three-year-old who will contest the early lead with Nibras Gold; recent form shows a placing at 12f on Good (3rd and 2nd in last two), suggesting he handles the conditions, but Charlie Fellowes' yard is winless in 12 runners over 14 days and the horse has yet to win.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in recent starts to demand respect — third last time out and a second two starts back give Tai Hang Pegasus solid placed form, he has experience over today's trip and going, and 19 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh. The main risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus are both confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a contested early pace over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Brighton. Nibras Gold, winner last time out and clearly at home on similar going (13 of 15 runs on comparable ground), will look to assert from the break, while Tai Hang Pegasus has the youth and recent course form to push for the lead. The duel between them should produce an honest, even gallop rather than a true scorching pace, but enough pressure to stretch any horse running beyond their stamina limits. This shape most strongly favours a forward-travelling prominent racer with proven stamina and the ability to slot just off the speed — horses who can track the battle and pounce without burning energy fighting for position in the early exchanges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus fight for the early lead, creating a genuine gallop that softens both front-runners late.
scenarios.body: The two leaders push each other through the race, and the horse sitting prominently just behind — conserving energy while the pace is set — emerges with a decisive finishing burst in the final two furlongs. Sarangpur, in excellent recent form with three wins at 12f on Good, is ideally profiled to track and overhaul a weakening pace-setter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Nibras Gold — establishes a clear lead early and Tai Hang Pegasus is unable or unwilling to match the initial surge, leaving the pace honest but uncontested.
scenarios.body: Nibras Gold, a proven course-distance type with excellent form on Good and coming off a recent win 26 days ago, controls the race in his own time and the closers simply have too much ground to make up. His age and experience at 8 mean he knows his job and can regulate the gallop to suit himself when left alone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners genuinely burn each other out and the pace is truly strong enough to bring hold-up horses into the race from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Maasai Mara or Bohemian Breeze, both genuine hold-up types, would find themselves in range if the leaders tie each other up; however, both have mixed recent form and Bohemian Breeze's best recent wins have come over shorter 10f, making a 14f late swoop uncertain. The probability is tempered by the fact that the pace, while contested, is unlikely to become truly extreme over this trip with just six runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is misjudged mid-race, the field compresses turning in and every runner has a shout in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slow-burning gallop that concertinas the field late would bring Brave Hunter — a horse with consistent placing form and a capable jockey in De la Sayette — into contention alongside any of the first three in the market. This scenario is the least probable given the clear pace dynamic at the front, but Brighton's undulating nature can occasionally produce a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus — watch which of the two front-runners actually secures the lead at the break; whoever is forced to settle second from the front will be racing outside their comfort zone and may fold turning for home.

Sarangpur — if Finley Marsh gets a clean prominent position tracking the pace in the first three, his in-form profile and Good-ground credentials make him the most dangerous stalker in the race; watch his position after the first two furlongs.

Bohemian Breeze — both recent wins came over 10f and today is unproven territory at 14f; if the pace is not strong enough to bring him into it late, the extra two furlongs could simply find him out before the line.

Brave Hunter — top weight by OR but the yard's 0/7 in 14 days is worth noting; a market move would suggest connections are confident the visor and the step up in trip will unlock improvement, so track any significant support before the off.

Maasai Mara — 55 days off the track and a modest similar-going record; William Carson is an experienced handler of Brighton's quirks but this horse needs everything to fall right and the fitness angle is a real question mark.

races.name: Jenningsbet Top Staff Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Handles good ground and has course-distance experience, but six-year-old's recent form figures of 870574 show consistency is lacking; a natural closer who will be forced to race in a more forward position than he prefers, reducing his ability to deliver a late run when the pace is likely to be modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a best recent finish of fourth, Alex The Great makes little appeal near the foot of the ratings here; he has run over today's trip and going, but a 135 lb burden compounds the task for a gelding whose recent form reads poorly throughout.

runners_data.name: Dogged
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with two placed efforts from ten recent runs on similar going, and William Carson's local-course knowledge is an asset; hold-up horse who will be anchored at the back of a slow-run race where little cut in the ground offers no help — needs a collapse from the front to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Ran second three starts back and returns on a quick turnaround having run over today's trip and going, with our rating nudging above his official mark — the concern is that his last two outings have brought only fifth and sixth.

runners_data.name: Foinix
runners_data.note: 45 days off the track for the Jim & Suzi Best yard which has returned just 0 winners from 3 in the last fortnight; hold-up type whose best Brighton run came over 12f but whose recent record on similar ground shows limited consistency, and a dawdling pace over 1m4f works against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Foinix nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, and having run over today's trip and going, he arrives on the back of a third last time out after a string of modest efforts — 45 days between runs is the one note of caution, but the 135 lb burden is manageable.

runners_data.name: Gearing's Point
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good ground at a previous start and brings the best OR in the field at 50, but ran just two days ago which is an obvious fitness query; confirmed front-runner who will get a dream uncontested lead, and while the [STYLE_FIT] tag notes a slight role displacement, this is essentially his ideal scenario if he has recovered.
runners_data.comment: Gearing's Point warmed up for this with a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, making her a solid danger at 135 lb; the chief concern is that she was sixth last time out just two days ago.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Ithaca
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 3-year-old dropping back to a trip slightly below her best distance range and carrying the apprentice allowance through Liam Wright; likely to slot in prominently behind Gearing's Point and is the one horse who could genuinely make a race of it at the head of affairs, though her form on Good ground is limited to just two runs.
runners_data.comment: Dream of Ithaca has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 49 by us against an official mark of 47, is marginally ahead of the assessor — yet five starts without a win in recent form and 59 days off the track are the key questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Lady Lauren
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly whose best form figures include a placing on soft ground, suggesting she benefits from ease underfoot that she will not get today; a true closer whose instinct will be to hunt the back markers, but in a slow-run race she will be held up in a position closer to midfield than she naturally wants, blunting whatever late kick she possesses.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a best recent finish of third, Lady Lauren faces a stiff task as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures; she has run over today's going before and 40 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Gearing's Point is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger to the lead, should control this 1m4f Brighton contest at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on Good to Firm ground. Dream Of Ithaca will likely sit prominently behind, creating a two-horse breakaway from the pack of hold-up types who fill the rest of the field. The hold-up brigade — Alex The Great, Dogged, Foinix, and Lady Lauren — will be bunched in behind with no pressure injected early, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to truly bring them into the race late. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Alex The Great and Lady Lauren are genuine closers who have been mapped to midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a lone, uncontested front-runner over a galloping 1m4f trip on fast ground is a classic setup for a made-all or prominent winner, with the hold-up horses denied the strong pace they need to close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gearing's Point Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Gearing's Point jumps cleanly and is allowed to control a steady-to-moderate tempo unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Gearing's Point sets the fractions exactly as he pleases, with Dream Of Ithaca the only horse in his vicinity but unlikely to press him hard enough to force a collapse; the 8-year-old showed he can win over this C&D trip and a solo lead role on Good to Firm suits him ideally.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca tracks Gearing's Point closely enough to mount a sustained challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: Dream Of Ithaca, the unexposed 3-year-old carrying 10lb less, presses the leader from the two-furlong marker and the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up from a slow early pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If Gearing's Point goes too soon and ties up in the final furlong, opening a gap for a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: A genuine collapse from the front is needed, plus a pick of trajectory through a moderate field; Dogged has the best course form of the closers and, having placed at this track, is the most likely beneficiary if the pace unravels.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Gearing's Point is outpaced early or suffers interference and the pace becomes chaotic.
scenarios.body: Without a controlling hand on the race, the moderate pace becomes irregular and unpredictable, leaving the outcome open to whichever runner handles the disruption best; the Tony Carroll pair Dogged and Alex The Great have the class of experience to capitalise but all hold-up types remain out of position.

watchPoints.text: Gearing's Point ran two days ago — monitor pre-race for any sign of fatigue or stiffness, as a sub-par lead horse who ties up early transforms the entire race shape.

Dream Of Ithaca is the only horse likely to track Gearing's Point, and if Liam Wright (5lb claimer) misjudges the fractions and lets the leader get too far clear at halfway, the hold-up horses will be racing for minor money.

Alex The Great and Lady Lauren are genuine hold-up horses who will struggle to get their natural position in what shapes up as a slow-run race — if either is seen further back than midfield, their chance of landing a blow is significantly diminished.

Dogged and Foinix are both trained by yards out of form in the last 14 days (Carroll 4/40, Best 0/3), which adds a layer of caution to relying on either as the hold-up type who can close late even if the pace does collapse.

The going report consistently describes 4:55 conditions as Good to Firm — faster ground favours horses who can control pace from the front, reinforcing Gearing's Point's tactical advantage and further undermining the hold-up runners' closing ability.

races.name: JenningsBet In Brighton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a recent course win (1st/7f/GOO) in good heart; Eve Johnson Houghton's T14 strike rate of 3/38 is modest but the horse's natural travelling style suits sitting just off a controlled pace, and Good to Firm ground is exactly what it wants.
runners_data.comment: Silver Trumpet arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a serious threat from stall seven carrying 135 lb — the worry is whether he can back up that victory after a patchy run of form before it.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer dropping back from a 2nd over 7f on Good ground last time; apprentice claimer Olivia Haines (7lb) helps at the weights, but from the rear North View needs Dion Baker to set a pressured tempo that simply may not materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in recent starts and drawn in stall two, North View returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before — his second last time out is the form to side with, and a rating of 76 makes him the one to beat here, albeit still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field and the pivotal pace-setter; recent form of 1-1-3-1 is strong, the 7f Good-ground distance is well within range, and William Carson's ability to judge pace from the front makes him the race's most important tactical player — quick back at 6 days but has been running frequently all season.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into eighth last time out on a quick six-day turnaround, Dion Baker finds this tough on our figures, ranked sixth of seven. He has winning form in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going, but the current trajectory is a concern.

runners_data.name: Serenity Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a recent win over 6f on Good and placed at 6f on the Standard surface; Tony Carroll's string is in form at T14 4/40, but the step back up to 7f on Good to Firm is a question mark given the horse's recent sprint trips, and it will need the pace to lift to deliver from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Serenity Dream arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, giving him sharp recent form, and he has experience of today's trip and going; the worry is that 130 lb is a stern burden to carry.

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a poor recent record (574676) and a very thin sim-going sample showing 0 wins from 15; Finley Marsh takes the ride and while the horse will aim to press Dion Baker, its lack of recent form in similar conditions makes it a significant each-way risk at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dontspoilasale nevertheless boasts distance and going experience, arrives fit on a 17-day break, and a rating of 76 suggests he's better than his official mark of 68 — though his persistent tendency to finish mid-pack is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose 2nd over 7f on Good ground in its recent history shows the distance and conditions suit; a 45-day break is worth monitoring for freshness, but Mark Loughnane's T14 2/17 is respectable and a horse that can sit handy behind a controlled pace has an obvious chance.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in recent starts — second last time out and third four starts back — but winless in his last six, and 45 days off the track adds a fitness query; has run over today's trip and going, though, and 128 lb from stall 4 gives him a workable profile.

runners_data.name: Just Jump
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse — most recently winning over 5f on Good — mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field is crowded with genuine backmarkers; only 2 days since its last run which is very tight, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) underlines that racing out of its natural role weakens its expected impact in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Back two days after finishing third last time out, Just Jump is quickly back up having won three starts back, but he ranks last on our figures in this field and the turnaround looks sharp — stall one and experience over today's trip and going offer slim consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no other natural pace-setter to challenge him, William Carson should be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Silver Trumpet, Dontspoilasale, and State Of Madness are all prominent-style horses who will press for early position behind him, creating a bunched, competitive pack through the early stages rather than a strung-out procession. North View, Serenity Dream, and Just Jump are the hold-up horses, though Just Jump has been redistributed to midfield on the map as the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — Just Jump is the one most likely pushed out of its true rearward position given the competition for that space. With Dion Baker able to set an uncontested, metronomic tempo on Good to Firm ground over 7f at Brighton, this race shape strongly favours front-running and prominently-placed runners who can travel into the race comfortably and are not dependent on a furious pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dion Baker Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker jumps well and is unchallenged early, setting a measured pace that suits gallopers over stayers.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker dictates from the front with William Carson controlling the tempo, ensuring no excess early speed burns the field out; horses who travel prominently into the race without being hard-ridden early are best placed. Silver Trumpet and State Of Madness, both prominent types with Good-ground course form, are ideally positioned to challenge if Dion Baker weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Upsets Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the three prominent horses push forward aggressively enough to lift the tempo and unsettle Dion Baker's rhythm through the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace would stretch the field and potentially expose Dion Baker before the finish, handing the initiative to a horse like Silver Trumpet or State Of Madness who can sit just behind and pounce. Both have shown the ability to deliver a late challenge off a genuine pace on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late finish and one of the backmarkers produces a powerful closing run.
scenarios.body: North View or Serenity Dream would need a strong gallop to generate the momentum required to reel in a settled leader from the rear, and with Dion Baker likely to control the fractions that scenario is unlikely to fully develop. Serenity Dream's recent course-winning form over shorter offers some upside if the tempo is misjudged and there is a true sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker is slowly away or the field races erratically with no one willing to commit, turning this into a slow-run sprint.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race would compress the field and turn the finish into a short sharp burst, making draw, athleticism and fresh legs more relevant than stamina or race position. Just Jump, with a win on similar going recently, could benefit if able to find a clear run from its redistributed midfield berth, though its natural hold-up style means it remains at a positional disadvantage regardless.

watchPoints.text: Dion Baker's jumping and early stride must be tracked — if William Carson gets a clean break and immediately settles in front without a challenge, the race is likely set up to play out from the front and this becomes the horse to beat.

Silver Trumpet, Dontspoilasale, and State Of Madness will all bid for the same prominent ground behind Dion Baker — watch the first furlong for jostling; if that group races too keenly in pursuit it could compromise their own finishing efforts.

Just Jump ran only 2 days ago and is being asked to race out of its natural hold-up role mapped to midfield — monitor paddock freshness and whether it can actually settle in a forward enough position to make its pace of late-run tell.

North View ridden by a 7lb claimer (Olivia Haines) from a hold-up position — watch whether the weight advantage allows it to creep into contention at the two-furlong pole if the pace does genuinely lift in the back straight.
Going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the card header showing Good — horses with firm-ground concerns should be monitored at the start for any signs of unease on the faster surface.
